name: Dressler & Kang Wool Overcoat
description:
A single-breasted overcoat in a dense charcoal melton wool, cut with the kind of long, clean line that makes a person look like they've made a decision. Peak lapels, two welted hip pockets, a single back vent. The lining is a deep burgundy silk-analog printed with a small geometric pattern — almost invisible until the coat swings open. Buttons are matte black horn.

Dressler & Kang occupy the upper edge of Tier 3 pricing — expensive enough to feel like an investment, not so expensive that it screams corporate. Their overcoats are worn by mid-level analysts who want to look serious without looking like a Vantablack ad, by architects and consultants, by the kind of people who own one very good coat instead of several mediocre ones. The silhouette is timeless in the way that only very well-cut things can be.
what_it_says: You understand quality without needing to announce it. You are probably the most competent person in the room.
worn_by: Tier 3 professionals who dress above their tier
story_hooks: A specific run of Dressler & Kang overcoats was commissioned by a law firm for their entire senior staff — six of those lawyers are now dead under unrelated circumstances.
The silk-analog lining pattern, examined closely, contains a repeating motif that an art historian recognizes as a pre-war encoded document format.
Dressler & Kang's tailoring shop on the Tier 3 commercial strip is a known dead-drop location — the owner knows nothing about it.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions ChemoShield BX-2 Dermal Toxin Barrier Implant

physical_description.visual_profile: A commanding single-breasted silhouette that elongates the wearer's frame. The coat drapes with architectural precision, creating a decisive vertical line from shoulder to knee. Peak lapels frame the chest with authority. The overall impression is understated power — someone who made their choices carefully and expects them to be respected.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not tight; structured through the shoulders with a subtle taper at the waist, then relaxed through the hips and thighs. Designed to layer over corpo business wear or street-tech without bunching. Length hits just below the knee for maximum stride coverage.
physical_description.primary_material: Dense charcoal melton wool — high-quality, tightly woven synthetic-wool blend with excellent drape and weight retention. Naturally resistant to wrinkles and urban grime.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost polished surface with subtle nap; dense enough to feel substantial without being heavy. The melton weave catches light uniformly, creating a matte, sophisticated finish. Interior silk-analog lining is smooth and cool against skin.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep charcoal gray-black as primary, with matte black horn buttons as tonal accents. Hidden burgundy silk-analog lining with small geometric print (visible only when coat opens or moves) provides a luxe secret — the kind of detail that signals intentionality to those who notice.
physical_description.closures: Six matte black horn buttons down the front; single-breasted configuration. Each button is substantial and slightly recessed, suggesting quality without ostentation.
distinctive_features: Two welted hip pockets (functional, visible seaming)
Single center back vent for stride mobility
Burgundy silk-analog lining with geometric jacquard pattern — visible detail that rewards inspection
Matte black horn buttons that age naturally over time
Internal construction visible at seams: precise tailoring, reinforced stress points
physical_description.tier_indicator: Upper Tier 3 — expensive enough to signal investment and taste, not so expensive that it broadcasts corporate wealth. Accessible to working professionals with disposable income and aesthetic conviction.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by mid-level analysts, architects, consultants, security detail with actual authority, and the kind of corpo who climbed through merit rather than family. The person wearing this coat made a decision and is comfortable with it. Street-smart professionals who understand that one excellent thing beats three mediocre things.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to broken-in. Dressler & Kang overcoats develop character with age — slight softening at stress points, patina on buttons, subtle sheen developing on high-contact areas. Even a well-worn example reads as intentional rather than neglected.
